Love for the Guru's Word, love of kindness to living beings, the praise of Parmatma — the person who does these deeds in this world (literally, having done these deeds),
To be imbued and attuned to the Word of the Shabad; to be kind and compassionate; to sing the Kirtan of the Lord's Praises - these are the most worthwhile actions in this Dark Age of Kali Yuga.
To be imbued and attuned with the Name, to be compassionate to life and to sing praises of God, these are the deeds worth doing in the Darkage.
O pandits! (Ratan) Love for the Guru's (sabdan) teaching, love of being kind, and uttering Vahiguru's (keertan) praise — such deeds are fit to (kritua) do in the Kali Yuga; and whoever does them —
F6E7: the doubt and attachment that have come there (that is, theirs) are wiped away.
In this way, one's inner doubts and emotional attachments are dispelled.
Thiswise doubt and attachments of his inner-dwelling are effaced.
(tatra) by doing them, doubt and attachment, and the state of no liberation too, are wiped away.
9VB6: To them Bhagvan appears pervading every place.
God is pervading and permeating all places.
My fortunate Lord is pervading all places.
They come to know Bhagvan as (ramanan) filling all places.
H4B9: Tuyan drisat = Your gaze (of grace). Amogh = never fruitless (amogh = unfailing). Rasna = tongue.
You dwell on the tongue of the saints; Your sight and Your gaze (of grace) are never fruitless.
So obtain the Blessed Vision of His Darshan; He dwells upon the tongues of the Holy.
See you the fulfilling vision of Him, who abides on the tongue of his saints.
They (drisat tuyan) behold the One whose sight is unfailing and who dwells on the tongues of the saints.
PDV8: Nanak (says:) O Hari! (Those saints) love to chant Your Name. ||8||
O Nanak, meditate and chant the Name of the Beloved Lord, Har, Har, Har, Haray. ||8||
O Nanak, recite you the Name of your Lord God Master, yea, the Beloved God.
Because those saints chant the Name "Hari Hari" of that (prian) Beloved Hari, the remover of pains. ||8|| ☬ Calling Vahiguru and the saints imperishable, he describes the world as ever-changing:
H4Y4: Ghatant = wane, perish. Deepan = islands, continents (dveep). Rav = the sun (ravi). Saseear = the moon (shashdhar = moon). Nakhyatr = stars (nakshatra). Gagnan = sky.
Beauty is perishable; the (seven) continents are perishable; the sun, moon, stars and sky are perishable;
Beauty fades away, islands fade away, the sun, moon, stars and sky fade away.
Perishable is beauty, perishable are the islands and perishable are the sun, the moon, the stars and the sky.

O brother! This beauty too wanes day by day — that is, it is ever-changing; and the seven continents too (ghatant) change; and (rav) the sun, (saseear) the moon, (nakhyatr) the stars and (gagnan) the sky too keep waning.
5LAL: Ghatant = wane, perish. Basudha = the earth (vasudha). Gir = mountain (giri). Tar = tree (taru). Sikhandan = lofty-peaked.
the earth, the lofty mountains and trees are perishable;
The earth, mountains, forests and lands fade away.
Perishable is the earth, mountains, trees and the three worlds.
Again, (basudha) the earth, (gir) the mountains, (tar) the trees, together (si) with the nine regions, wane — that is, keep changing.
0QAF: wife, son, brother and relatives are perishable;
One's spouse, children, siblings and loved friends fade away.
Perishable are wife, sons, brothers and friends.
Again, the (hitan) love of (lalna) wife and (sut) son, brother and other relatives wanes in old age, at the time of death, or in misfortune.
N0Z3: Ghatant = wane, perish. Kanik = gold. Maanik = pearls.
gold, pearls — all the forms of Maya — are perishable.
Gold and jewels and the incomparable beauty of Maya fade away.
Perishable are the beauteous gold, jewels and wealth.
(Kanik) Gold, and (maanik) — the big stone among rubies is called a maanik — these are forms of (maya) deception; all these things wane.
50S4: Only the imperishable Gopal Prabhu is not perishable,
Only the Eternal, Unchanging Lord does not fade away.
Imperishable is only the Immovable Lord.
The One Gopal, the Unshakeable, who is (keval) the pure form, never wanes.
3WTS: and, O Nanak, His holy company too lasts for ever. ||9||
O Nanak, only the humble Saints are steady and stable forever. ||9||
Everstable are the Lord's holy men, O Nanak.
Sri Guru ji says: being of His form, His saints too are forever of lasting form. ||9|| ☬ Sri Guru ji says: the one with whom Madhav is well pleased receives these marks of dharma.
USZM: Not delaying in earning dharma, delaying in sins,
Do not delay in practicing righteousness; delay in committing sins.
Tarry not in practising righteousness, Tarry you only in committing sins.
They make no (bilamb) delay in doing dharma, and delay in sinful deeds.
MDEA: Drirrant = making firm, settling in the mind, chanting. Tajant = giving up.
making the Name firm (in the heart) and giving up greed,
Implant the Naam, the Name of the Lord, within yourself, and abandon greed.
Shedding your avarice, implant you the Lord's Name within you.
They make the Name firm in the heart and give up greed.
MFUG: going to the shelter of the saints and destroying sins — these marks of dharma
In the Sanctuary of the Saints, the sins are erased. The character of righteousness is received by that person,
Seeking the protection of the saints, the sins are washed off.
Taking the saints' shelter, they destroy sins; such marks of dharma come to them —
B04H: Jih = on whom. Maadhvah = the husband of Maya, the Lord of Maya, Parmatma (Madhav). ||10||
O Nanak! are gained by the person on whom Parmatma shows mercy. ||10||
O Nanak, with whom the Lord is pleased and satisfied. ||10||
With whomsoever the Lord is mightily pleased, he is blessed with the attributes of religion, O Nanak.
Sri Guru ji says: those with whom the Lord of Maya is pleased. ||10||
4BSH: Mirat = perishable things. Alap = little (alpa). Alap budhyan = a person of shallow intellect. Rachant = stays absorbed, stays intoxicated. Binod = play (vinod = amusement). Saahan = zest, delight.
The person of shallow intellect stays absorbed in attachment to perishable things, intoxicated in play and delights with a wife.
The person of shallow understanding is dying in emotional attachment; he is engrossed in pursuits of pleasure with his wife.
The man of paltry intelligence is perishing in worldly love and is engrossed in pleasure with his wife.
Enchanted by (mrit) perishable things, the being of (alap) meagre intellect is absorbed, (saahan) full of ego, in the (binod) pleasures of (banita) wife and the rest.
J7Y1: youth, strength, earrings of gold (and the like),
With youthful beauty and golden earrings,
(Worldliness has so much clung to him, that) he looks adorned with young age, gold earnings,
The state of youth, and (bahikram) strength, and earrings of gold —
132Y: Bachitr = of many kinds. Bastra = clothes. Ityant = in this way. Byaapitan = takes hold.
mansions of many colours, beautiful clothes — in these ways Maya takes hold of them (casts its influence).
wondrous mansions, decorations and clothes - this is how Maya clings to him.
Especially, one shines with palaces and clothes of many kinds. In this way the being, utterly caught in Maya, suffers the pains of birth, death and the rest.
59V0: Bho = O! Bhagvaanae = to Bhagvan. Namah = salutation. ||11||
Nanak (says:) O Imperishable One! O Support of the saints! O Bhagvan! We bow to You (You alone save from the influence of Maya). ||11||
O Eternal, Unchanging, Benevolent Lord God, O Sanctuary of the Saints, Nanak humbly bows to You. ||11||
O Eternal Master, O Auspicious Lord and the protection of the saints, Nana pays homage to You.

So, O Unshakeable One, (saran sant) form of the saints' support! Sri Guru ji says: O Bhagvan, my salutation to You. Meaning, let the being pray to Vahiguru like this; or he himself prays: O Hari, protect this being from Maya. ||11|| ☬ He speaks of beings' receiving the pairs of opposites:
0YFT: Harkhan = happiness, joy (harsh). Sogan = worry, grief (shok).
(Where there) is birth, (there) is death too; if there is happiness, there is sorrow too; if there are pleasures (of worldly things), there are diseases (arising from them) too.
If there is birth, then there is death. If there is pleasure, then there is pain. If there is enjoyment, then there is disease.
If there is birth, then there is death also, if weal, then woe also and if indulgence, then aliment as well.
If this being is born, dying comes with it; if there is joy, grief too surely comes; again, if there is pleasure, disease too follows after.
VBNH: Ta = and, also. Naanha = small. Moochan = big.
Where there is loftiness, lowliness also comes; where there is poverty, greatness too can come.
If there is high, then there is low. If there is small, then there is great.
The lofty become low and the tiny very great.
If there is high, there is low too; if one is (naana) small, one also becomes (moochan) big.

055V: Ta = and, also. Heenan = lowliness, disgrace.
Where there is rule, there is pride too; where there is pride, there is disgrace too.
If there is power, then there is pride. If there is egotistical pride, then there will be a fall.
Power breeds ego and pride must have a fall.
When there is rule, there is also becoming low; and from honour, (abhimaanan) dishonour too sometimes comes.
W2V9: Maargan = path (maarg). Pravirt maarag = the path of engaging in the world.
So on the road of the world, everything has an end (too).
Engrossed in worldly ways, one is ruined.
Being engrossed into the worldly ways one is ruined.
So, O brother, while living on the path of worldly engagement, in the end there is only destruction.
D0RU: Asthiran = lasting for ever. Bhajnaasnan = bhajan-asan, the food of remembrance (asan = food) (ash = to eat). ||12||
What lasts for ever is devotion to Parmatma alone, which (can be done with the support of) the holy company. (So,) O Nanak, (give your soul) the food of remembering Bhagvan. ||12||
Meditating and vibrating on the Lord of the Universe in the Company of the Holy, you shall become steady and stable. Nanak vibrates and meditates on the Lord God. ||12||
O Nanak, contemplating the Word Lord in the saints' society and securing a seat by the Auspicious Lord's meditation.
The remembrance of Gobind done in the company of the saints alone is lasting. So such saints alone are imperishable, because those saints have taken the (asnan) food of remembering Bhagvant. ||12||
7L4W: Kirpant = grace (kripa). Hareean = Hari, Parmatma (Hari). Tat giaan = understanding of reality, true understanding of spiritual life.
Where Parmatma's grace is, a person's intellect gains understanding of true life,
By the Grace of God, genuine understanding comes to the mind.
By God's grace, real understanding enters man's mind.
When Hari's (kirpant) grace is on this being, then true knowledge of the self (tat) arises in their (mat) intellect.
8JE1: Bigseedhy = stay blossoming. Budha = wise people (budh). Kusal = peace, bliss.
(such an intellect) becomes a home of peace; wise people (of such intellect) stay always blossoming.
The intellect blossoms forth, and one finds a place in the realm of celestial bliss.
His intellect blossoms forth and he secures a seat in celestial bliss.
From that, attaining the (kusal thaanan) form of well-being, the intellect (bigseedhy) blossoms.
Y43M: Basyint = under control. Rikhian = the senses (hrishik). Tiaag = giving up.
By giving up pride, their senses stay under control,
The senses are brought under control, and pride is abandoned.
He controls his sense organs and his ego in stilled.
They give up (maanan) ego, and the (rikhian) senses come under control.
MHWV: Drirr = make firm. Sant = peace-giving. Giaanan = understanding of spiritual life.
Their heart stays (always) cool; this peace-giving knowledge stays firm within them.
The heart is cooled and soothed, and the wisdom of the Saints is implanted within.
Confirmed in gnosis, through the saints, his mind is cooled.
When one makes firm in the heart, through the saints, the knowledge of one's true form, then one's heart becomes cool.
8D75: Rahant = remains, comes to an end. Leena = absorbed.
The birth (and death) of such people, absorbed in the sight of Parmatma, comes to an end,
Reincarnation is ended, and the Blessed Vision of the Lord's Darshan is obtained.
Absorbed in the God's vision, his comings and goings are ended.
Absorbed in Hari's (daras) form, one becomes free of birth and death.
20RP: O Nanak! Within them the instruments of the Bani of Parmatma's praise (always) play. ||13||
O Nanak, the musical instrument of the Word of the Shabad vibrates and resounds within. ||13||
The flute of the Name, O Nanak, plays within him.
Sri Guru ji says: in their heart plays the (beena) instrument of the Guru's Word. ||13||
LXXA: Kahant = say. Gunant = reflect. Guneea = thoughtful people. Baala = children, students. Bahu bidh = in many ways. Bahu prakaara = of many kinds.
What the Vedas say, learned people reflect on in many ways and methods, and (their) students listen.
The Vedas preach and recount God's Glories; people hear them by various ways and means.
The Vedas narrate and ponder over God's virtues and good people hear them by various means and ways.
(Guneea) The virtuous, (gunant) reflecting, expound the Vedas in many ways, and (baala) seekers hear them in many ways.
4JYN: But those on whom Parmatma's grace falls make the highest learning (of remembering Parmatma) firm (in their hearts).
The Merciful Lord, Har, Har, implants spiritual wisdom within.
To whom-so-ever the Lord God is merciful, He implants His knowledge in his mind.
Those on whom Hari is merciful make learning firm in every way.
A6PR: O Nanak! Those fortunate people (always) ask only for the gift of the Name from the Giver, the Guru-Parmatma. ||14||
Nanak begs for the Gift of the Naam, the Name of the Lord. The Guru is the Great Giver, the Lord of the World. ||14||
Nanak begs for the bounty of the Lord's Name and the Guru-God blesses him with it.
Sri Guru ji says: so we ask Vahiguru for the gift of the Name, because the Giver of the gift of the Name is the One Gopal and the True Guru alone. ||14|| ☬ He gives teaching to remove worry:
MGY3: Chinta = worry (about providing for). Pit = father. Bhraatah = of brothers. Lok kah = of people.
Worrying for mother, father and brother is useless,
Do not worry so much about your mother, father and siblings. Do not worry so much about other people.
Be not too much anxious about your mother, father, and brother and don't entertain any anxiety for your friends.
This being should not worry about mother, father, brother and the rest, nor is it fitting to worry at all about people.
BN7Z: Banita = wife (vanita). Sut = son (suta). Meetah = of friends.
wife, son, friends and other people — who are (our) relatives because of being engaged in Maya — any kind of worry for them is useless.
Do not worry about your spouse, children and friends. You are obsessed with your involvements in Maya.
Nor need you be over anxious for your wife, sons and friends: being over occupied with them amounts to establishing relation with mammon.

Nor should one worry about wife, son, friends and the rest, because the involvement of these relatives comes only from the bond of Maya — meaning, they love a person because of Maya. When misfortune falls, no one asks after them.
JSNK: O Nanak! The sustainer of all beings, the ocean of mercy, is the One Bhagvan, Akal Purakh alone. ||15||
The One Lord God is Kind and Compassionate, O Nanak. He is the Cherisher and Nurturer of all living beings. ||15||
The One Fortunate Lord alone is compassionate, O Nanak. He alone is the Cherisher of all the beings.
Sri Guru ji says: it is the One Bhagvan Purakh who, merciful to all, sustains all beings. Knowing this, O brother, be free of all worry. ||15||
XX3Y: Anity = not lasting, useless. Vitan = wealth (vitta). Chitan = thinking.
Wealth does not last for ever; (so) thoughts (of wealth) are a useless (effort), and (making) many kinds of hopes for wealth is (also) useless.
Wealth is temporary; conscious existence is temporary; hopes of all sorts are temporary.
Unstable are the riches, unstable are the mind's dreams and unstable are the hopes of many sorts and kinds.
O brother! This (vitan) wealth too is (anity) false, and the mind too is unstable — meaning it does not stay the same; and the many hopes of many kinds for things of many sorts are also unstable.
MUVJ: Hetan = attachment. Ahan bandhan = bound by ego, bound by "I". Malnan = dirty. Bikaaran = bad deeds, sins.
Because of attachment to things that do not last, the being bound by ego wanders for the sake of Maya and does dirty, evil deeds.
The bonds of love, attachment, egotism, doubt, Maya and the pollution of corruption are temporary.
Illusory are the bonds of worldly love, self-conceit, doubt, worldliness and filthy sins, with which the mortal has bound himself.
Because, through (anity) false (hetan) love for those things or relatives, the being bound by ego, in doubt, is caught up in the dirty vices born of Maya.
X0X3: Jathraagan = the fire of the womb. Maleen budhyan = of dirty intellect.
The person of dirty intellect wanders through countless births and does not remember the fire of the (mother's) womb (which must be endured on entering a birth).
The mortal passes through the fire of the womb of reincarnation countless times. He does not remember the Lord in meditation; his understanding is polluted.
The man of pollute understanding contemplates not his God and passes through the fire of many times in womb.
Because of that, they burn in the fire of the mother's womb and wander through countless births, because a being of dirty intellect never remembers Vahiguru.
AXKR: Karat = show. Maia = mercy (mayas = joy, pleasure). Patit = great wrongdoers (patita), fallen (into vices) (pat = to fall). ||16||
Nanak (prays:) O Gobind! Show mercy, and grant beings the holy company, where even great wrongdoers escape. ||16||
O Lord of the Universe, when You grant Your Grace, even sinners are saved. Nanak dwells in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy. ||16||
Says Nanak, when You, O Lord, showed mercy, You saved even the sinners, through the saints' society.

Sri Guru ji says: but, O Gobind, when You show grace to this being, then You bring even the sinner to the company of the saints and redeem them. ||16|| ☬ He speaks of the overwhelming pains of household life:
AUCV: Girant = falling. Gir = mountain (giri). Dedeepy = burning, blazing. Baisvaantrah = fire (vaishvaanar).
Falling from a mountain into the netherworld, burning in blazing fire,
You may drop down from the mountains, and fall into the nether regions of the underworld, or be burnt in the blazing fire,
If one drops down from a mountain to fall into the underworld, burns in the blazing fire,

Someone may (girant) fall from a (gir) mountain and (patit) land in a (paataalan) low place, and even that is not such pain; and if one throws the body into (dedeepy) blazing fire and burns it, that pain too is not such —
YJNS: Agaah = deep. Toyan = (toya) water. Tarangan = waves (tarang = a wave). Dukhant = causing pain. Grah = house (griha). Grah chinta = attachment to Maya.
being swept away in the waves of deep waters — (to escape) the worry of the house (attachment to Maya) and the pains of birth and death,
or swept away by the unfathomable waves of water; but the worst pain of all is household anxiety, which is the source of the cycle of death and rebirth.
or is swept off by the unfathomable water waves; of all these, the worst pain is of the household care, which is the root cause of births and death.

being (bahant) swept away in the (tarangan) waves of fathomless (toyan) water is not such pain as the pain of worry for the house. For that pain is soon over; and what is the fruit of that worry? That one keeps undergoing birth and death for ever.
HY9G: Na sidhyate = does not succeed. Svajanah = good people. Asthambhan = (stambh) pillar, support, refuge. ||17||
countless such (hard) practices do not succeed. O Nanak! The being's lasting support is the Guru's Word alone, which is found in the holy company. ||17||
No matter what you do, you cannot break its bonds, O Nanak. Man's only Support, Anchor and Mainstay is the Word of the Shabad, and the Holy, Friendly Saints. ||17||
Inspite of adopting various means, one can snap not its bonds, O Nanak. One's only support, help, and the mainstay is the instruction of the friendly saints.

Sri Guru ji says: the attainment of release from the pains of this house is not gained even by doing countless practices. So, O brother, what saves this being from these pains in all three times is only the (sabad) teaching of the saints, the good people — it is the (asthambhan) support; meaning, the Guru's teaching, taken up —
AAVT: Ghor = terrible (ghor = awful). Hatyan = killing, murder. Daaridran = sloth, poverty (daaridrya). Bikhyaadan = disputes, strife (vishaad).
Terrible pain and trouble, countless killings (committed), the poverty of birth after birth, great strifes — all these
Excruciating pain, countless killings, reincarnation, poverty and terrible misery
The dreadful diseases, the sins of various murders, the penury of many births and immense miseries,
Even if terrible pains afflict one, and one has committed countless killings, is poor through births, and is also stricken with great (bikhyaadan) grief —
D801: Sagal = all (sakal). Paavak = fire (paavak). Kaast = wood (kaashth = a piece of wood). Bhasman = ash (bhasman = ashes). Karoti = (karoti) makes. ||18||
O Nanak! are wiped away by remembering Parmatma's Name, as fire turns wood to ash. ||18||
are all destroyed by meditating in remembrance on the Lord's Name, O Nanak, just as fire reduces piles of wood to ashes. ||18||
are all destroyed, by contemplating the Lord's Name, says Nanak, just as the fire reduces to ashes the piles of wood.
By remembering the Name of the One Hari, all those sins and pains are wiped away. How are they wiped away? Sri Guru ji says: just as a little fire burns a great deal of wood to ash. ||18||
21GL: Andhkaar = darkness (andhakaar). Prakaasan = light (prakaash). Ramant = remembering, keeping in mind. Agh = sin (agh = a sin).
By remembering Parmatma's Name the darkness (of ignorance goes and) there is light (of understanding of spiritual life). By keeping Prabhu's virtues in mind, sins are destroyed.
Meditating in remembrance on the Lord, the darkness is illuminated. Dwelling on His Glorious Praises, the ugly sins are destroyed.
Remembering the Lord, inner darkness is illumined and singing His praises, the sins are destroyed.
In the inner mind that holds the darkness of ignorance, by remembering Vahiguru the light of knowledge arises, and by uttering the virtues of that Hari all sins go away.
PTKP: When Prabhu's Name dwells in the heart, even the messengers of death are afraid; that person becomes one who does very pure deeds.
Enshrining the Lord deep within the heart, and with the immaculate karma of doing good deeds, one strikes fear into the demons.
Enshrining God in the mind and doing supremely immaculate deeds, one is able to smite death's courier with great fear.
When the form of Vahiguru dwells in the heart, even the messengers of death become fearful of that person, for they do most pure deeds.
MPQG: Srota = listener. Amogh = fruitful, never failing to give fruit (amogh). Amogh darsanah = His sight is fruitful.
The (round of) birth and death of the one who listens to Prabhu's praise comes to an end; Prabhu's sight never fails to give fruit — it gives countless comforts.
The cycle of coming and going in reincarnation is ended, absolute peace is obtained, and the Fruitful Vision of the Lord's Darshan.
Hearing the God's Name, man is rid of coming and going, obtains, all comforts and sees the Lord's accredited vision.

That person, becoming a listener of Hari's praise, becomes free of birth and death. They receive a multitude of comforts, so the sight of that person too is unfailing — meaning, by seeing them, beings' wishes are fulfilled.
H9BG: Saran jogan = able to help those who come to His shelter. Sant pria = beloved of the saints. Khemaan = well-being, peace (kshem). Karoti = (karoti) does. ||19||
O Nanak! That Bhagvan who is the beloved of the saints and able to help those who come to His shelter gives (His devotees every) comfort. ||19||
He is Potent to give Protection, He is the Lover of His Saints. O Nanak, the Lord God blesses all with bliss. ||19||
He, the Illustrious Lord, O Nanak is worthy of giving protections, is the Lover of His saints and blesses all with bliss.

Bhagvan, the beloved of the saints, able to give shelter, whose meditation's greatness was told above — Sri Guru ji says — that same Vahiguru (khemaan) protects His servants. ||19|| ☬ He speaks of the greatness of serving the True Guru:
H66S: Paachhan = behind. Karoti = (karoti) makes. Agrneevah = those who go in front (agrani = a leader).
That Prabhu makes those who walk behind into leaders; He fulfils the hopes of the hopeless.
Those who were left behind - the Lord brings them to the front. He fulfills the hopes of the hopeless.
The Lord brings to the fore those that are left behind and fulfills the hopes of the hopeless.
O brother! The One who puts those behind in front and fulfils the hopes of the hopeless —
XJ8G: (By His mercy) the pauper becomes wealthy. That Master is able to destroy the diseases of the sick.
He makes the poor rich, and cures the illnesses of the ill.
The poor, one, He makes rich and destroys He the disease of the diseased one.
the penniless (bhayan) become wealthy, and He destroys the disease of the sick.
LPUS: Prabhu gives His devotees the gift of His devotion, His Name, and the praise of His virtues.
He blesses His devotees with devotion. They sing the Kirtan of the Praises of the Lord's Name.
His devotees, he blesses with his devotion and they sing the Lord, Name and praise.
He gives the gift of devotion to the devotees; by His gift the saints sing the kirtan of the virtues of Ram's Name.
TFUE: Kin na = what not? (that is,) everything. Labhyate = is found. ||20||
The all-pervading Prabhu is the giver of all gifts. O Nanak! Through service of the Guru, what is not gained (from Him)? ||20||
O Nanak, those who serve the Guru find the Supreme Lord God, the Great Giver||20||
O Nanak, a few only, by Guru's service, find the Beneficent Transcendent Lord Master.
Sri Guru ji says: through the grace of the Giver, Parbraham Purakh, and by serving the Guru, what (kin) do people not find? Meaning, they attain dharma, wealth, desire and liberation. ||20||
PD4K: Adharan = without support. Dharan = support. Narharah = Parmatma. Naam narharah = Parmatma's Name.
Parmatma's Name gives support to the unsupported, and is the wealth of the poor.
He gives Support to the unsupported. The Name of the Lord is the Wealth of the poor.
He gives support to the supportless. The Name of the Man-lion incarnate Lord is the wealth of poor.
It is the (dharan) support for upholding the (adharan) unsupported, and for those who are penniless their wealth is the Name of Narhari — meaning Hari is the wealth of those who own nothing.
A9TL: Kesvah = Parmatma (the One with long hair). (Keshav: from kesha, hair.)
Gobind is the Master of the masterless, and Keshav-Prabhu is the strength of the weak.
The Lord of the Universe is the Master of the masterless; the Beautiful-haired Lord is the Power of the weak.
The world-Sustainer is the Master of the masterless and the Beauteously-haired Lord is the Power of the powerless.
That Gobind is the Master of the masterless, and Keshav is the form of strength for the weak who lack strength.
ZBCL: Bhoot = beings (bhoot). Achut = the imperishable Prabhu (achyut). Deen = poor. Baandhav = kin, relative. Daamodarah = Parmatma (daaman = a string; daaman-udar).
The imperishable Prabhu is merciful to all beings and is the kinsman of the poor.
The Lord is Merciful to all beings, Eternal and Unchanging, the Family of the meek and humble.
The Imperishable Lord, with a string round His belly, is merciful to all the beings and the relation of the meek.

That Unshakeable One is merciful to all (bhoot) beings and is Damodar, the (baandhav) kinsman — that is, protector — of the humble. When mother Yashoda tied Krishan Dev ji by the belly to a mortar with a rope, from then His name was Damodar; meaning, He is thus under the control of His devotees.
0UYB: Sarbagy = (sarvagya) knower of every heart. Pooran purakh = all-pervading. Bhagat vachhal = lover of devotion. Karuna-mayah = (karuna = compassion) the form of compassion, the form of mercy.
The all-pervading Bhagvan knows the heart of all beings, loves devotion, and is the home of compassion.
The All-knowing, Perfect, Primal Lord God is the Lover of His devotees, the Embodiment of Mercy.
The Omniscient, Omnipresent and Omnipotent Auspicious Lord is the Lover of His saints and the Embodiment of compassion.
The One who is thus all-knowing is Bhagvan, the Being filling all; He alone is the (vachhal) beloved of the devotees, the form of grace.

7QM1: Ghat ghat = in every heart. Baasudevah = Parmatma.
Parmatma, Parbraham Parmesar, dwells in every heart.
The Supreme Lord God, the Transcendent, Luminous Lord, dwells in each and every heart.
The Luminous Lord, the Supreme Master and the Great God abides in every heart.
That Vasudev is dwelling in every heart; so such is Parbraham Parmeshvar.
KQD3: Jaachant = asks (yaach = to beg). Prasaadan = kindness, grace (prasaad). ||21||
Nanak asks the merciful Narayan for this gift of grace: that He may never be forgotten by me, never be forgotten. ||21||
Nanak begs for this blessing from the Merciful Lord, that he may never forget Him, never forget Him. ||21||
Nanak begs but this grace from the Merciful Master, that he may forget Him not, yea, forget Him not ever.
Sri Guru ji says: I beg for the (prasaadan) grace of that Merciful One, that Narayan may never be forgotten by me in mind, body and speech. ||21|| ☬ He sets out the manner of praying:
JWDA: Samarthan = ability, strength. Purkhotaman = the highest Being, Parmatma.
O supreme, highest Akal Purakh! (Within me) there is neither the ability (to remember You), nor am I a servant, nor is there love (for Your feet) within me.
I have no power; I do not serve You, and I do not love You, O Supreme Sublime Lord God.
O my most sublime Lord, I have no power, neither do I serve you nor do I love You adequately.
O brother! Pray thus before that Vahiguru: O Vahiguru, highest of beings! In me there is neither the ability of spiritual practice, nor the spirit of a servant, nor is there love in me.
BRGH: Tav = Your (tav). Prasaad = by the grace (prasaadena). Guran = the greatest of all. ||22||
O merciful Hari! O Guru-Hari! Nanak (Your servant) remembers Your Name (only) by Your mercy. ||22||
By Your Grace, Nanak meditates on the Naam, the Name of the Merciful Lord, Har, Har. ||22||
By your grace, O my merciful Guru-God, Nanak meditates on the Lord's Name.
Sri Guru ji says: so, O Hari, (guran) greatest of all, supremely merciful! By Your grace alone we ever remember Your Name, Hari. ||22||
9FFD: Bharan pokhan = sustaining and nourishing. Bisraam = resting place, support. Chhaadan = clothing (chhaadan = clothing).
He sustains and nourishes all beings, and gives gifts of clothing, shelter and the like.
The Lord feeds and sustains all living beings; He blesses them gifts of restful peace and fine clothes.
The Lord feeds and sustains the beings and blesses them with the bounties of rest and raiments.

Again, what is that Vahiguru like? ☬ First He fills beings' bellies with every kind of taste and (pokhan) nourishes them; then He gives a place to sleep, a bed and the like, and (chhaadan) clothes and such to wear.
ER7T: Srijant = creates (srij = to create). Chatur = wise, able. Chetanah = conscious, able to perceive everything (chit = to perceive).
The able Parmatma, the form of consciousness, (alone) gives (beings) the excellent human birth.
He created the jewel of human life, with all its cleverness and intelligence.
He has created the invaluable, wise and clever human body.

Out of all life-forms He has (srijant) created and given the highest, (ratan) priceless human birth, which is supremely able for the (chetanah) remembrance of that Hari. Meaning: the ordinary affairs of life are achieved in other life-forms too, but remembrance of the Name is not done in others; it is done only through this birth.
B945: Prasaadah = by the grace. Anity = not lasting. Nirmoh = saved from attachment. Te = those people. ||23||
By the grace of that Prabhu, the form of bliss, beings live in comfort. O Nanak! Those beings who remember that Hari stay unattached to this perishable creation. ||23||
By His Grace, mortals abide in peace and bliss. O Nanak, meditating in remembrance on the Lord, Har, Har, Haray, The mortal is released from attachment to the world. ||23||
By God's grace, the mortals abide in peace and pleasure. O Nanak, contemplating on the Lord God's Name, man's love with the perishable world is severed.

Again, all these lives live in comfort by the (prasaadah) grace of that Vahiguru, the form of bliss. Sri Guru ji says: so in this human birth, those who in every way remember the Name of Hari, who makes all green — they have become unattached to the perishable creation of the world; meaning, giving up worldly attachment, they have become lovers of the Name. ||23|| ☬ Those pandits asked about the fate of kings; to this he says:
AN6U: Para poorben = in former births. Bhunchante = enjoy (bhuj = to possess), enjoy ownership. Maheepate = lords of the earth, kings (mahee = earth; maheepati = king).
By virtue of the good deeds done in former births, kings enjoy the ownership (of kingdom and estate here).
The kings of the earth are eating up the blessings of the good karma of their past lives.
The Kings of the earth eat the fruit of the charities of the past births.
O brother! The pleasures given for the merit done in former births, kings (bhunchante) enjoy as lords of the (mahee) earth.
ATYN: Bipreet = perverse (vipreet). Maarat lokah = the mortal world, the world. Maarat = (martya = mortal) perishable. Dukh = (duhkh) pain. ||24||
But, O Nanak, those whose intellect becomes perverse (because of those pleasures) here in the perishable world suffer pain for a long time. ||24||
Those cruel-minded rulers who oppress the people, O Nanak, shall suffer in pain for a very long time. ||24||
Through evil intellect in this mortal world, they shall suffer agony for a long time, O Nanak.

But those whose intellect, through those pleasures, becomes perverse in this (maarat) mortal world — through it they kill people; meaning, they cause the people pain. Sri Guru ji says: they go to the next world and suffer the fruit of those sins in hells and other pains for a long time. ||24||
9WEG: Britha = empty, deprived. Anugrahan = grace (anugraha = a favour). Jasy = whose (yeshaam). Ridantarah = rid-antarah, in the heart.
The people who are deprived of Gobind's mercy, whose hearts are empty of His remembrance,
Those who meditate in remembrance on the Lord in their hearts, look upon even pain as God's Grace.
He, within whose mind is the Lord's meditation, deems pain to be God's grace.
Those kings who are (britha) empty of Gobind's grace, and in whose heart there is a gap between them and the remembrance of Parmeshvar's praise — meaning, they do not remember —
NQZ2: Aarogyan = healthy, free of disease. Bisimrite = forget. Karuna mayah = karuna-mayah, the form of compassion, the form of mercy (karuna = compassion). ||25||
even those healthy people are gravely ill, because they are forgetting Gobind, the form of mercy. ||25||
The healthy person is very sick, if he does not remember the Lord, the Embodiment of Mercy. ||25||
The apparently healthy one is in fact gravely diseased, If he remember not God, the Embodiment of mercy.

Even if they are healthy, know them to be gravely ill, because they have forgotten the form of compassion; meaning, they always burn with the fever of the mind. ☬ Second meaning: the saints in the depths of whose heart is the remembrance of Vahiguru know even (britha) pain as Gobind's grace. Even if they are gravely ill in body, they still consider themselves healthy — meaning, they know the self to be unattached — because they always especially remember the form of compassion. ||25||
36ZH: Ramanan = chanting. Kevalan = (keval = solely) only. Sudharman = the highest dharma. Deh dhaaranah = one who has a body, human beings.
Only singing (God's) praise is the highest dharma of human beings.
To sing the Kirtan of God's Praises is the righteous duty incurred by taking birth in this human body.
The sublime duty of assuming human body is simply to recite and sing the Lord's praise.
To (ramanan) speak and hear the praise of the (kevalan) pure, one-without-a-second Parmeshvar — this alone is the highest dharma of taking on a human body.
JUVS: Amrit = the water that gives spiritual life. Tripyate = are satisfied (trip = to be contented; tripyati). ||26||
O Nanak! The saints are never satisfied drinking the water of Parmatma's Name, which gives spiritual life. ||26||
The Naam, the Name of the Lord, is Ambrosial Nectar, O Nanak. The Saints drink it in, and never have enough of it. ||26||
Nectar-sweet is the Lord's Name, O Nanak, the saints in-drink it and long for more and more.
Sri Guru ji says: the saints, knowing the Name of such a Narayan to be nectar, are never satisfied as they drink it. Meaning, their love for remembering the Name is always there. ||26||
R58A: Sahan = bearing (sahan). Seel = sweet nature (sheel). Sahan seel = (sahan sheel = patient, forgiving). Sam = equal. Mitrasy = of a friend (mitrasya). Durjanah = bad people (durjan).
To the saints, friend and wicked person are alike. Bearing the wrongs of others becomes their nature.
The Saints are tolerant and good-natured; friends and enemies are the same to them.
Tolerant and sweet-tempered are the saints and to them the friends or the evil-seekers are alike,
The nature of those saints is (sahan seel) to bear harsh words.
CBEG: Aavadh = weapons, arms (aayudh). Uptisatte = come near (upatishthati = comes near). ||27||
O Nanak! Friends come to them bringing food of many kinds, but slanderers come with weapons (to kill them) — (they look on both with the eye of love). ||27||
O Nanak, it is all the same to them, whether someone offers them all sorts of foods, or slanders them, or draws weapons to kill them. ||27||
and even those who offer the them varieties of food or who becoming slanderers, draw weapons to kill them; O Nanak.

Sri Guru ji says: friends are present (tisatte) near (up) them bringing food of many kinds, and slanderers and wicked people are present nearby with (aavadh) weapons of many kinds to kill them. But to the saints, being patient by nature, (sa) that friend and that enemy are both alike. ||27||
7F7H: Tiraskaar = dishonour (tiraskaar). Bhavant = happens (bhavati, bhavatah, bhavanti; bhu = to become). Maan bhanganah = disrespect, insult.
Those (people) can never be dishonoured; they can never be insulted,
They pay no attention to dishonor or disrespect.
The saints suffer not disrespect, nor meet they with dishonour.
Those saints are not (tiraskaar) dishonoured in this world, and in the next world too their honour is not broken — that is, there too they are honoured.
KY38: their glory never fades, and the pains of the world cannot touch them —
They are not bothered by gossip; the miseries of the world do not touch them.
They become not inglorious, nor do the worldly pains touch them.
Even if they go to the netherworld or any other place, they are not without glory, because the pains of the world cannot (pohant) touch them.
F97X: Japant = (japanti) chant. Mil = joining. Se praanee = those people. ||28||
those who chant Gobind's Name, joining the holy company. O Nanak! Those people dwell (always) in peace. ||28||
Those who join the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, and chant the Name of the Lord of the Universe - O Nanak, those mortals abide in peace. ||28||
They, who, meeting with the saints' society, recite the World-Lord's Name, those mortals abide in peace.

Those who, joining the company of such saints, chant Gobind's Name — Sri Guru ji says — those beings who chant the Name dwell in comforts, or are worthy of comforts. ||28|| ☬ He describes the saints in the form of kings:
8ZSG: Saina = army (sena). Saadh samooh = all the holy ones, the saints. Soor = warriors. Sannaahan = armour (sannaah = armour). Tan = on the body.
The saints are an army of unconquerable warriors. A humble nature is the armour on their body;
The Holy people are an invincible army of spiritual warriors; their bodies are protected by the armor of humility.
All the saint are an unconquerable army of the heroes, who have doused their body with the coat of arms of humility.
(Saadh) The divine qualities are the army of those saints, the unconquerable warriors, and the humility they have taken on is their (sannaahan) armour.
1X2M: Aavadhah = weapons (aayudh). Kar = hand (kar). Charmanah = shield, hide (charman). Kar charmanah = the shield in the hand.
singing Gobind's virtues is the weapon they carry; the shelter of the Guru's Word is the shield in their hand.
Their weapons are the Glorious Praises of the Lord which they chant; their Shelter and Shield is the Word of the Guru's Shabad.
Their weapons and shelter are the recitation of the Lord's praises and the Guru's word is the shield in their hands.

To (ramanan) speak and hear Gobind's virtues — this is the (aavadhah) weapon they have taken up; and to protect themselves from the enemies that are vices, they have taken the (ot) shelter of the (charmanah) shield of the Guru's (sabad) teaching.
PPCJ: Aarooṛte = ride. Asv = (ashva) horses. Naagah = elephants (naag).
The saints keep seeking the road (to union) with Parmatma — this is, as it were, their riding on horses, chariots and elephants.
The horses, chariots and elephants they ride are their way to realize God's Path.
To realise the Lord's path, is their riding the horses, chariots and elephants.

Those who (bujhante) understand Prabhu's path have (aarooṛte) mounted these very (asv) horses, chariots and (naagah) elephants. Or: mounted on the horse of hearing, the chariot of reflection and the elephant of deep contemplation — that is, taking these up — they (bujhante) understand Prabhu's form by this path; meaning, through it they come to direct realisation of Prabhu.
GXM7: Bicharte = move about. Satr = enemies (lust and the rest) (shatru). Dhaayante = charge, attack (dhaavanti).
With (the help of) Parmatma's praise, the saints charge the army of enemies (lust and the rest), and (so) move about fearless (among them).
They walk fearlessly through the armies of their enemies; they attack them with the Kirtan of God's Praises.
They walk fearlessly among the army of their enemies and charge them with the Lord's praises.
The saintly warriors move about fearless in the demonic army of the enemy that is attachment, and (dhaayante) charge — that is, attack — with Gopal's kirtan.
RA9M: O Nanak! The saints bring under their control those five thieves who are conquering the whole world. ||29||
They conquer the entire world, O Nanak, and overpower the five thieves. ||29||
They conquer the whole world and overwhelm the five thieves as well, O Nanak.
They conquer the whole world. Sri Guru ji says: in this way they (karoti) bring the five (taskarah) thieves, lust, anger and the rest, under their control — that is, into subjection. ||29||
T4YJ: Mrig trisna = (the deer's thirst) a mirage: sandy land that looks like a river of water in the sun's heat. The deer, frantic with thirst, runs towards the water; the mirage keeps moving further ahead, and so the deer writhes and dies (mrigtrishna = mirage). Gandharab nagaran = a city dwelling in the sky; like the mirage, this too is only an illusion that a city is standing in the sky (gandharva-nagar). Drum = tree (drum). Rach = taking as real, accepting as true.
The person of bad intellect takes the mirage, the castle in the air and the shade of a tree to be real.
Misled by evil-mindedness, mortals are engrossed in the mirage of the illusory world, like the passing shade of a tree.
Owing to evil-intellect, man is engrossed in optical illusion, phantom city and the shade of a tree.

Just as in a mirage in the desert, when the sun's rays strike, the deer, deluded, sees water and runs towards it, but that water is false; and just as a city of the Gandharvas appears in the sky through illusion but is in reality unreal; and just as, taking the shade of a tree to be permanent, (rach durmatih) one of evil intellect becomes absorbed in it — that is, loves it; meaning, beings of evil intellect are loving these unreal things in just this way.
JY5D: Tatah = there, in the same way (tatah = for that reason). Mithya = perishable, false (mithya = to no purpose). Durmatah = of bad intellect (durmati). ||30||
Attachment to the perishable family is of the same kind. O Nanak! (Giving it up, the saints) remember Parmatma's Name. ||30||
Emotional attachment to family is false, so Nanak meditates in remembrance on the Name of the Lord, Raam, Raam. ||30||
Similarly, the love of family is false, so, Nanak meditates on the Name of his Lord Master.

In the same way, the family to which this being is attached is false. The saints, knowing it to be (mithya) false, give up love for it and always remember the Name of Ram, the (Ram) all-pervading form. ||30|| ☬ He shows the manner of prayer:
XNBQ: Na-ch = and not, nor. Nidhaan = treasure. Nigaman = the Vedas (nigam). Gungy = knower of virtues (gungya).
Neither am I a treasure of Vedic learning, nor am I a judge of virtues, nor do I have the praise of Parmatma.
I do not possess the treasure of the wisdom of the Vedas, nor do I possess the merits of the Praises of the Naam.
I possess not the treasure of the Veda's knowledge, nor am I a man of merit, nor sing I the praise of the Lord's Name.
O Hari! I am not a treasure of (nigaman) Vedic learning, nor (nach) a knower of virtues, nor have I sung the kirtan of the Name.
XL8D: Kanth = throat. Chanchal = quick, nimble. Chatur chaaturah = wisest of the wise. Chaaturah = wise.
There is no fine melody in my throat, nor am I quick and very wise.
I do not have a beautiful voice to sing jewelled melodies; I am not clever, wise or shrewd.
I am not blessed with the throat of singing invaluable melody, nor am I clever, wise and shrewd.
Nor (nach) is the jewel of melody in my throat; nor am I nimble in bodily dealings; I am not clever in speech, nor clever in intellect. Meaning, I am so without virtue.
1U80: Saadhsang = in the holy company. Khal = fool (khal). ||31||
Maya is gained by effort according to past fortune (I do not have that either). (But,) O Nanak, coming into the holy company, (even) a fool (becomes) a pandit (this is my support too). ||31||
By destiny and hard work, the wealth of Maya is obtained. O Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, even fools become religious scholars. ||31||
Through good fortune and concerted effort, are obtained such treasures, Nanak by the saints' society even the fools become scholars.

By the rising of past fortune and by effort this being gains Maya; or, when merits come forth, divine qualities are gained. And then even a (khal) fool lacking the deeds described above becomes a pandit through the true company — that is, becomes endowed with the knowledge of Braham. As it says: ☬ "He alone is a pandit who takes off the bundle of the three qualities." ☬ "He alone is a pandit who instructs his own mind." ☬ I am lacking in such learning and other virtues. O Vahiguru! So, in grace, give me the company of the saints. ||31||
CGLM: Kanth = throat. Ramneey = beautiful (ramaneeya). Hast = (hast) hand. Hast ooch = the gomukhi, the rosary bag: a bag shaped like a cow's mouth in which the rosary is placed and turned. By Hindu scripture it may not touch the ground; the chant is done with the hand raised to the breastbone, hence the name "hast ooch" (hand raised). Dhaarnee = placing.
The person who makes the utterance (from the throat) of Parmatma's Name the beautiful rosary of their throat, and makes the holding of love (in the heart) their rosary bag,
The mala around my neck is the chanting of the Lord's Name. The Love of the Lord is my silent chanting.
To recite the Lord's Name, is the rosary around my neck and to love the Lord is my secret telling of it.

The chanting of Ram's Name in the throat is the (ramneey) beautiful rosary; this is the (hast ooch) gomukhi they have taken up — they chant with love placed within; meaning, holding love, they remember the Name.
0GCA: Jeeh = tongue. Bhan = utters, bhanai. Nandanee = one who pleases (nandan = pleasing). Nain nandanee = the one who pleases the eyes, Maya. Nain = (nayan) eyes. ||32||
the person who utters the Bani of praise with their tongue — they are saved from the influence of Maya. ||32||
Chanting this most Sublime Word brings salvation and joy to the eyes. ||32||
Reciting with my tongue the sublime word of the Guru, I have been saved from mammon, the joy of the eyes.
By the excellent (salok) praise of Vahiguru that we (bhan) utter with the tongue, (udhranan) redemption has come from Maya, which delights the eyes. ||32||
TXUT: Heenasy = empty. Bhrastanah = of corrupt intellect.
The person who is empty of the True Guru's teaching — the life of that one of corrupt intellect deserves reproach.
That mortal who lacks the Guru's Mantra - cursed and contaminated is his life.
The mortal, who is without the Guru's instruction, his life is accursed and contaminated.
The being who is without the Guru's (mantr) teaching — cursed is the birth of that one of corrupt intellect.
L1N4: Kookarah = dog (kukkur). Sookarah = pig (sookar). Gardhabhah = donkey (gardabh). Kaakah = crow (kaak). Tul = equal (tulya). Khalah = fool (khal). ||33||
(Know) that fool to be equal to a dog, a pig, a donkey, a crow, a snake. ||33||
That blockhead is just a dog, a pig, a jackass, a crow, a snake. ||33||
He, the blockhead is equal to a dog, a swine, an ass a crow and a snake.

That foolish person is equal to dogs and pigs, donkeys, crows and snakes. Meaning, the person without the Guru's mantra will keep wandering through such life-forms for ever. Or: they are not even equal to these, because each of these has one virtue: in the dog, devotion to its master; in the pig, cleaning the village; in the donkey, giving up the taste of the tongue; the crow keeps friendship with those of its kind; the snake gives up its venom at the name of its elders — but in the self-willed are the opposite qualities. ||33|| ☬ Question: how may a being be freed from the fear of Yama's messengers? To this he says:
MCN8: Charnaarbind = charan-arbind, lotus feet (charan-aravind). Arbind = lotus flower (aravind).
The person who settles Parmatma's Name in their heart, who remembers Parmatma's lotus feet,
Whoever contemplates the Lord's Lotus Feet, and enshrines His Name within the heart,
Whosoever contemplates the Lord's lotus feet, enshrines His Name in his mind,
The person who holds Vahiguru's lotus feet in the heart and remembers the Name —

S805: who, joining the holy company, sings Parmatma's praise — O Nanak! The messengers of Yamraj cannot (even) look at that person (because vices do not come near them). ||34||
and sings the Kirtan of His Praises in the Saadh Sangat, O Nanak, shall never see the Messenger of Death. ||34||
and, associating with the saints, sings God's praise, he does not countenance myrimidons of death, O Nanak.

who goes into the holy company and sings the kirtan of Hari's praise with their speech — Sri Guru ji says — Yama's messengers do not look at that person; meaning, the fear of birth and death leaves their heart. ||34||
XY6R: Wealth and beauty are not very hard to find, nor is the kingdom of heaven.
Wealth and beauty are not so difficult to obtain. Paradise and royal power are not so difficult to obtain.
Not difficult to obtain are wealth and beauty. Nor is it difficult to obtain the sovereignty of paradise.
So, O brother, for this being the attainment of wealth and beauty is not rare, nor is the kingdom of heaven rare.
YS84: Binjanan = tasty foods, spiced dishes eaten with bread (vyanjan). Svachh = clean (svachchh). Ambarah = clothes (ambar).
Tasty spiced foods are not hard to get, nor are clean, neat clothes.
Foods and delicacies are not so difficult to obtain. Elegant clothes are not so difficuilt to obtain.
Not difficult to obtain are viands and dainties, nor it is difficult to obtain elegant raiments.
Eating foods of many tastes, (binjanan) sweet, salty and the rest, is (nach) not rare, and wearing (svachh) spotless clothes is not rare either.
7PT7: Sons, friends, brothers and relatives are not very hard to come by, nor are the affections of a wife.
Children, friends, siblings and relatives are not so difficult to obtain. The pleasures of woman are not so difficult to obtain.
Not difficult to obtain are the sons, friends, brothers and kinsmen, nor it is difficult to obtain revelments of women.
Having sons and friends, brothers and other relatives is not rare, and enjoying pleasures with women is not rare either.
QKMH: Becoming wise by gaining learning is not very hard either, nor is it hard to be clever and sharp-witted (with the help of learning).
Knowledge and wisdom are not so difficult to obtain. Cleverness and trickery are not so difficult to obtain.
Not difficult to obtain is accomplishment of learning. Not difficult to obtain is dexterity and cleverness.
Being (prbeenan) skilled in learning is not rare; again, being clever in speech and intellect, and nimble in body — that too is not rare.
J3XW: Yes, O Nanak! Only Parmatma's Name is hard to gain. The Name is found only in the holy company (but it is found when) Parmatma's mercy comes. ||35||
Only the Naam, the Name of the Lord, is difficult to obtain. O Nanak, it is only obtained by God's Grace, in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy. ||35||
But difficult to obtain is only the Lord's Name, O Nanak, It is obtained by the Lord's grace in the saints' society.

Sri Guru ji says: O brother! The Name of the One Bhagvan alone is rare; that Name is found from the true company, and that true company is (labdhin) attained by Prabhu's grace. ||35|| ☬ He describes where the Named One, Vahiguru, dwells:
PJ5N: Jat katah = wherever. Tatah = there. Jat katah tatah = everywhere. Marat = (martya) the mortal world, the earth. Payaal = the netherworld.
O Nanak! The person who has seen (that Parmatma) in heaven, the mortal world, the netherworld — everywhere,
Wherever I look, I see the Lord, whether in this world, in paradise, or the nether regions of the underworld.
Wherever I see, whether in elysium, on this mortal world or in the under-word, there I see my Lord.
O brother! Heaven and the (marat) mortal world, the earth, and the netherworld — wherever one (drisatan) looks —
LA43: Ramanan = pervading. Chhep = (kshep) trouble, slander, ego; vice. Lipyate = is stained. Lep = smear, impurity. ||36||
(sees) the One who is all-pervading, the Sustainer of the earth — He is not stained by the smear of vices. ||36||
The Lord of the Universe is All-pervading everywhere. O Nanak, no blame or stain sticks to Him. ||36||
Nanak, the Lord is pervading everywhere. No blame and blot attaches to Him.

the saints see, with the eye of spiritual knowledge, that Gobind who (ramanan) pervades all. Sri Guru ji says: that is why those saints are not stained by the (chhep) blemish of (lep) attachment. ||36|| ☬ The last line is to be read with the first: Sri Guru ji says, when Hari and the True Guru, the form of Hari, are merciful —
BAET: Bikhya = poison. Bhayant = becomes (bhavati, bhavatah, bhavanti). Amritan = giving spiritual life, making immortal. Drustaan = one who hates, one who opposes. Sakha = friend. Svajanah = sva-janah, one's own people, close relatives.
(then) poison becomes nectar for them; enemies become their friends and close relatives,
Poison is transformed into nectar, and enemies into friends and companions.
Contemplating God, poison turns into nectar and enemies into comrades and friends,
poison becomes nectar, and the wicked who are enemies become beloved kin, or friends of friends — that is, the closest of one's own.
2TMH: pain and trouble become comfort; if they (once) lived frightened by countless fears, they become fearless,

and pain turns into pleasure and the awestricken become fear-free.

The shelterless find place of rest in the Name, when Guru, the embodiment of the Lord God, becomes merciful, O Nanak.

4WZE: Sarab = all beings. Seel = peaceful nature, pure life. Paavan = making pure (pu = to make pure; causative paavayati).
The Prabhu who gives a peaceful nature to all beings gives me that same peace; the One who is able to make all pure is my purifier too;
He blesses all with humility; He has blessed me with humility as well. He purifies all, and He has purified me as well.
He, who blesses all with humility, has also blessed me with humility as well. The Purifier of all has purified me too.
Vahiguru, who gives (seel) peace to all, will give me peace too, and the One who makes all pure will make (maman) me pure too.

The Prabhu who is able to create all beings is my Creator too. O Nanak! That Prabhu is not stained by the smear of vices. ||38||
The Creator of all is the Creator of me as well. O Nanak, no blame or stain sticks to Him. ||38||
The Creator of all has created me as well. Nanak no accusation or stigma clings to Him.

The One who is the Creator of the whole universe is my Creator. 9CCA: Seetlan = cool. Chandr devah = the moon god, the moon. Baavan chandanah = vaaman chandan, white fragrant sandalwood.

nor can the winter season give (such) coolness, O Nanak, (as the) coolness and peace the Gurmukh holy ones give. ||39||

YDEB: Mantran = a word to be chanted to please a deity. Dhyaanan = fixing the attention absorbed in something (dhyaan).

VJT0: Gyaanan = understanding (gyaan). Sam = equal. Jugat = the way of living life.
seeing comforts and pains as the same, and living a pure life free of enmity;

He who deems pain and pleasure alike and whose way of life is immaculate and uninimical,
Those saints, through the vision of knowledge, stay the same in comfort and pain; and their pure way is this: that they stay free of enmity towards all.
HUJ3: having love and fellow-feeling for all beings, and staying free of the five vices, lust and the rest;

He, who is king to all the beings and overcomes his five deadly sins,
They are merciful to all beings and are (bivarjitah) free of the five faults, lust, anger and the rest.
AHSR: making Parmatma's praise the support of life, and staying as unstained by Maya as the lotus flower by water;

They give teaching seeing friend and enemy alike, and in their heart there is (bhaavnee) faith in devotion to Bhagvant.
FREZ: Srot = hearing. Sravanan = ears (shravan). Aap = self-centredness. Tyaag = giving up. Renukah = the dust of the feet.
not listening to others being slandered with one's own ears, and, giving up self-centredness, becoming the dust of everyone's feet —

Who hears not another's slander with his ears and stilling his self-conceit, becomes the dust of all.

whosoever has these six qualities, O nana, he is named the friendly8 saint and the perfect person.

Fraud, accusations, millions of maladies, offences, filthy sins,

doubt, emotional attachment, pride, dishonor and intoxication with Maya
doubt, dishonour, ego and absorption is worldly valuables

who sings Gobind's virtues every day — that person alone becomes pure. ||42|| ☬ Meaning, becomes free of the vices described above.

P85Q: Karan kaaran = the root of the world. Arath = things (artha).

O emotional attachment, you are the invincible warrior of the battlefield of life; you totally crush and destroy even the most powerful.
O worldly love, you are the invincible hero of the battlefield. You completely crush even the very powerful ones.

O attachment, warrior (ajit) unconquered by anyone in (sangraaman) battle! What are you like? You have crushed many very mighty ones; meaning, you made even Vasishth and others distraught at the death of their sons.

You fascinate even the heavenly heralds, celestial musicians, gods, mortals beasts and birds.
The gans, like Nandi and Bhringi, and the gandharvas, and all the gods, and humans, beasts and birds — you (bi) especially enchant all of these.

0EMZ: Chit haranan = one who beguiles the mind (hri = to captivate). Gamyan = reaching (gamya). Seel = pure conduct (sheel). Bidaaranah = destroyer (vid = to tear in pieces).

2RWM: Tav = your (tav). Bimunchit = release is gained. ||46||

O ego, (mool) cause of birth and death, (paapaatma) form of sin!

The only Physician is the Supreme Lord, the Transcendent Lord God. Nanak worships and adores the Lord, Har, Har, Haray. ||49||
