In the inner mind full of the darkness of ignorance, the light of knowledge arises like millions of suns.
9579: Nanak prays: (the person on whom) the Guru-Parmatma becomes merciful. ||64||
prays Nanak, when the Guru, the Lord, becomes Merciful. ||64||
when the Guru-God becomes merciful, prays Nanak.
Sri Guru ji says: when Hari and the Guru become merciful. ||64||

4N91: Sang = with, in the company. Udharnan = (uddharan) redemption. Braham = Parmatma. Braham karam = the work of remembering Hari's Name. Ji = who, the one who.
The person who is complete in the work of remembering Hari is the true Brahmin; in their company (others too) can be redeemed.
Associating with the Brahmin, one is saved, if his actions are perfect and God-like.
One is saved in the company of the Brahman. But Brahmin is he, who is brimful with the Godly deeds.
Through the company of those Brahmins who are complete in the Brahmin's work of studying the Vedas and the rest, the being is redeemed.
3S2J: Aatam = one's self, one's mind (aatman). Ratan = dyed. Gahante = (gachchhanti) go, pass through life. Nar = those people. Nihphalah = (nishphala = fruitless) fruitless. ||65||
(But,) O Nanak, the people whose mind is dyed in the world go (from the world) fruitless. ||65||
Those whose souls are imbued with the world - O Nanak, their lives are fruitless. ||65||
The persons, whose soul is imbued with the world, they, O Nanak depart all fruitlessly.
Those who, in the world, take up love (aatam ratan) for the body alone — meaning, who are proud of being Brahmins by birth alone — Sri Guru ji says: the birth of those people is fruitless. ||65||
9G66: Par = another's. Darab = wealth (dravya). Hirnan = stealing (hri = to steal). Kah = for, for the sake of. Sarab = all, words of many kinds. Jeea kah = for the sake of life, to sustain life, for a livelihood.
The people who, for the sake of sustaining their own life, steal others' wealth, put obstacles in others' work, speak words of many kinds,
The mortal steals the wealth of others, and makes all sorts of problems; his preaching is only for his own livelihood.
Man steals others wealth, commits many sins and all his sermonizing is for his livelihood.
(Ucharnan) Again, the beings who steal others' wealth and put obstacles in others' work, and utter every kind of speech for their livelihood —
F7HH: Lau = may I take. Laee = may I take. Atipat = (a-tipat) hunger, discontent. Maae = Maya. Sa = they, those people. Sookarah = pigs (sookar). ||66||

in whose mind there is (always) hunger for Maya, who under the sway of craving (keep thinking only) "let me take, let me take (more Maya)" — those people do the deeds of pigs (pigs always eat filth). ||66||
His desire for this and that is not satisfied; his mind is caught in Maya, and he is acting like a pig. ||66||
His mercurial desire is satiated not, his mind is absorbed in riches and he does the deeds of a swine.
They go about for the sake of the (lau) heap of craving; because of this their mind is unsatisfied with Maya — that is, it is never full. Those people do deeds like pigs. ||66||
X8HY: Mate = intoxicated (masta). Samev = absorbed (sam-eva), together with. Samev charnan = with the feet themselves. Bhai = fearsome, terrible. Dutarah = hard to cross (dustar).
The people who, intoxicated (in the remembrance of Prabhu), stay absorbed (in Prabhu's feet) cross the fearsome and impassable (world).
Those who are intoxicated and absorbed in the Lord's Lotus Feet are saved from the terrifying world-ocean.
They, who are intoxicated with God and merge in His feet, are ferried across the aweful and arduous world ocean.
The people who have become (mate) intoxicated (samev) wholly and surely in Vahiguru's feet are redeemed from the fear-giving, impassable ocean of the world.
Y2GN: Paatik = sins (paatak = a sin). Saadh sangam = the company of the Gurmukhs. Sansayah = doubt (sanshay). ||67||4||
O Nanak! There is no doubt (at all) that the company of such Gurmukhs is able to remove countless sins. ||67||4||
Countless sins are destroyed, O Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy; there is no doubt about this. ||67||4||
Associating with the saints, O Nanak, millions of sins are destroyed. There is not even an iota of doubt about this.

Sri Guru ji says: the conclusion of the whole teaching is this — the (sangam) meeting with the saints removes countless sins; that is, through the company of the saints alone all sins go away. There is no doubt in this; that is, it is true. ||67||4|| ☬ When in this way Sri Guru ji had taught the pandits Hari Lal and Hari Krishan through sixty-seven saloks and destroyed their attachment, they were pleased and prayed: "In Your grace, tell us some more nectar-like discourse, by which identification with the body may go." Sri Guru Arjan Sahib ji, knowing them to be full of love, uttered the Bani named Gatha, showing the impurity of the body and the glory of the saints:
DYNQ: Gatha = an ancient Prakrit language in which words of Sanskrit, Pali and other tongues are found written. Buddhist scriptures such as the 'Lalit Vistar' are in this language. Gatha = praise (gatha = a religious verse; gai = to sing).
The Bani 'Gatha' (discourse) of Guru Arjan Dev ji.
J62L: Akal Purakh is One, and is found through the grace of the True Guru.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but One God. By the True Guru's grace He is obtained.
QY95: Karpoor = camphor (karpoor). Puhap = pushp, flower (pushpa). Paras = touching (sprish = to touch). Dehan = body.
Musk, camphor, flowers and other perfumes become dirty on touching the human body.
Camphor, flowers and perfume become contaminated, by coming into contact with the human body.
Camphor, flowers and perfumes become filthy by coming in contact with the human body.
O brother! (Karpoor) Musk-camphor, (puhap) flowers and other fragrant things become dirty on touching this human body.
B1DC: Maja = marrow, the fat of the body (majjan = marrow of the bones and flesh). Rudhir = blood (rudhira). Drugandha = stench. Ath = even so, on top of this. Agyaanno = the ignorant person. ||1||
(In the human body) are marrow, blood and other foul odours; even so, O Nanak, the ignorant person takes pride (in this body). ||1||
O Nanak, the ignorant one is proud of his foul-smelling marrow, blood and bones. ||1||
The unwise one is proud of marrow, blood, foul odour and bones.

Again, it is full of (maja) marrow and (rudhir) blood and stench. Sri Guru ji says: this ignorant being, having got such a dirty body, (ath) even then (garben) is proud. Meaning, one should not be proud of this dirty body. ☬ The authority of Sri Guru Granth Sahib ji, as it says: ☬ "Excrement, bones and blood, wrapped in skin — ☬ over this one has set up pride."
FHFT: Parmaano = (paramaanu = an atom) the smallest particle, a fine speck that cannot be divided. Parjant = (paryant) the furthest limit, the final boundary. Deep = islands (dveep = an island). Loa = worlds. Sikhandanah = (shikharin) mountains.
O Nanak! If a person, becoming the tiniest atom, could go over all the continents, worlds and mountains as far as the skies
Even if the mortal could reduce himself to the size of an atom, and shoot through the ethers,
If by becoming subtle like an atom one crosses through the firmament, continents, the worlds and its regions,
Even if this being, taking a form as subtle as an atom through the power of occult powers, (goes) into the seven worlds in the sky and the continents with their regions —
NWJT: Gachhen = by going. Nain bhaaren = nain bharen, in the blink of an eye. Nain bhaar = netra bhar, the time of the blink of an eye, a moment. Na sidhyate = does not succeed. ||2||
and return in a single blink of an eye, (even with such occult power) their life is not fruitful without the Guru. ||2||
Worlds and realms in the blink of an eye, O Nanak, without the Holy Saint, he shall not be saved. ||2||
in the twinkling of an eye; even then, O Nanak, he is emancipated not without the saint.
and, (gachhen) going, returns in the flicker of the eyes — Sri Guru ji says — even so, without the company of the saints, the being never attains liberation. ||2||
8R9Q: Sat = true, certain (satya). Marano = death (maran). Drisatten = what is seen, this visible world. Mithia = perishable, false (mithya).
Know the coming of death as certain; this visible world is (surely) perishable (it keeps company with no one).
Know for sure that death will come; whatever is seen is false.
Know if for certain that death is true and all that is seen is perishable.
O brother! Know dying to be true, because the world of names and forms that is seen is all false.
FH5Y: Keerat = praise (keerti). Chalantho = goes (chalati, chalatah, chalanti). Saadh sangen = through the holy company (saadhu sangena). ||3||
Nanak says that only the praise of Parmatma, sung with the support of the holy company, goes with (a person). ||3||
So chant the Kirtan of the Lord's Praises in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy; this alone shall go along with you in the end. ||3||
Recite you the Lord's praise in the society of the saints, O Nanak this alone shall go with you.
Sri Guru ji says: the kirtan of Gopal — that is, uttering His praise — done through the company of the saints goes with one; meaning, this alone is true. ||3||
VFKJ: Chit = (chitta) mind. Isat = beloved (ishta). Mitrekhu = among friends (mitreshu).
Maya keeps (a person's) mind wandering in (attachment to) dear friends and relatives. (And because of the wandering they find no peace.)
The consciousness wanders lost in Maya, attached to friends and relatives.
The mind seeks after riches, the loved friends and kinsmen.
This Maya has made beings' minds wander (khu) among beloved friends and relatives — that is, in attachment to them.
GC3S: Labdhyan = can be found, worth finding. Sukh asthaanan = the place where peace is found (sukh sthaan). ||4||
O Nanak! The place where peace is found is (only) the remembrance of Parmatma, which can be gained through the holy company. ||4||
Vibrating and meditating on the Lord of the Universe in the Saadh Sangat, O Nanak, the eternal place of rest is found. ||4||
Contemplating God, the Word-Cherisher, in the saints' society, O Nanak, the eternal place of rest is obtained.
Sri Guru ji says: so, O brother, by keeping the company of the saints and remembering Gopal, the being (labdhan) gains their own true form, the place of peace. ||4||
UXHL: Mailaagar = the plant that grows on the Malaya mountain, sandalwood (malayaagra). Sangen = through the company (sangena). Birakh = (vriksha) tree.
Through the company of sandalwood, the neem tree becomes sandalwood itself,
The lowly nim tree, growing near the sandalwood tree, becomes just like the sandalwood tree.
Associating of sandal, the tree of Azadirachta indica too becomes as sandal.
Example: just as, through contact with Malayagar sandalwood, the neem and other bitter trees too become sandalwood —
0HSF: Nikat = near (nikate). Ahanbudh = because of an intellect full of ego (aham buddhi). Bohate = becomes fragrant. ||5||
but, O Nanak, the bamboo living near the sandalwood does not become fragrant because of its own stiffness. ||5||
But the bamboo tree, also growing near it, does not pick up its fragrance; it is too tall and proud. ||5||
The bamboo also dwells near, however, being arrogantly minded it is perfumed not, O Nanak.

but the bamboo living right near that sandalwood, full of the four faults of height, pride, hollowness, destroying its own kind, knots and the like, does not become sandalwood. ☬ Example: in the same way, even with the company of the saints, this being-as-bamboo, full of such faults as the height of ego, the knots of crookedness, the hollowness of being empty of good virtues so that teaching does not stay, and the destroying of its own kind which is opposing everyone, does not become fragrant with devotion; meaning, it does not attain goodness. And those free of these faults, even those of low caste like cobblers and Bhils who are like the neem, become the very form of the saints by keeping the true company. ||5||
54AP: Gatha = praise (gatha = a religious verse; gai = to sing). Gunph = to string together, to compose poetry (gumph = to string together, to compose). Kathan = discourse (katha). Mathan = to crush, to destroy (manth = to crush, destroy). Mardanah = is crushed (mardan).
Composing the stories of Parmatma's praise crushes and destroys a person's ego.
In this Gaat'haa, the Lord's Sermon is woven; listening to it, pride is crushed.
In this Gatha dialect (God's gospel) is weaved the wisdom, reflecting over which one's ego is crushed.

In this (gatha) Bani — meaning, by implication, all Bani concerned with Parmeshvar, in which the story of Gopal's praise is (gunph) strung together — by (mathan) reflecting on it, body-pride and the other vices are (mardanah) destroyed; meaning, the reflective person becomes free of pride.
X7TS: Hatan = are destroyed. Baane = (baan) arrow. Prahaaranah = by shooting (praharan = striking, throwing). ||6||
O Nanak! By shooting the arrow of Parmatma('s praise), all five enemies (lust and the rest) are destroyed. ||6||
The five enemies are killed, O Nanak, by shooting the Arrow of the Lord. ||6||
By charging the arrows of God's Name, O Nanak, the five enemies are slain.
Sri Guru ji says: by (prahaaranah) shooting the arrows that are Hari's Names — that is, by chanting them — the five enemies, lust and the rest, are (hatan) destroyed. ||6||
BVA9: Saadh = (saadhu) the Guru, the Gurmukh. Pantha = path (pantha). Lahantha = find.
The Guru's words (of Parmatma's praise) are the path to peace, but these words are found by good fortune.
The Words of the Holy are the path of peace. They are obtained by good karma.
The saint's words are the paths of peace. They are obtained by good destiny.
The word of the saints is the (pantha) path to gaining peace; one of great deeds — that is, of great fortune — (lahantha) attains it.
7D9G: Rahanta = ends, comes to an end. Ramanan = remembrance. ||7||
O Nanak! By singing Parmatma's praise, (the round of) birth and death comes to an end. ||7||
The cycle of birth and death is ended, O Nanak, singing the Kirtan of the Lord's Praises. ||7||
Reciting the Lord's praises, one's coming and goings are ended.
Sri Guru ji says: by (ramanan) uttering the kirtan of that Hari, the being becomes free of birth and death. ||7||
YQP3: Bhurijen = crumbling. Ped = tree. Sampata = with the wealth (sampad = wealth). Ped sampata = with the wealth of the tree, with the branches of the tree.
(Just as a tree's) leaves crumble and fall (from the tree) (and cannot be joined again to the tree's branches),
When the leaves wither and fall, they cannot be attached to the branch again.
when leaves wither and fall, they can attach not again to the tree branch.

Just as the leaves of trees (jhareeyan) fall (bhurijen) each in their own season, and those fallen leaves are not joined again to the (sampata) branches of those trees; meaning, those leaves are carried by the wind in all four directions and perish —
QN19: Bikhamta = hardship (vishamata). Bahant = suffer (pain), wander (vahanti; vah = to suffer, experience). Baasro = day (vaasar). Rainee = night (rajani). ||8||
(so) O Nanak, people without the Name suffer pain, and wander day and night through (one) birth (after another). ||8||
Without the Naam, the Name of the Lord, O Nanak, there is misery and suffering. The mortal wanders in reincarnation day and night. ||8||
Nanak, without the Name, there is suffering and day and night one wanders in species.
Sri Guru ji says: so this being, without chanting the Name, wanders day and night through (bikhamta) hard — that is, crooked — life-forms. ||8||
7GZ3: Bhaavnee = faith (bhaavana = feeling of devotion, faith).
Through the holy company, faith (in Parmatma's Name) is gained by great good fortune.
One is blessed with love for the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, by great good fortune.
Through great good fortune, one is blessed with the love for the saints' society.
Only a person of great fortune (labhantan) attains (bhaavnee) faith in the company of the saints.
XECY: Ramanan = remembrance. Saagar = ocean (saagar). Biaapanah = (vyaap = to pervade) can overpower. ||9||
O Nanak! Through remembrance of Parmatma's Name and virtues, the world-ocean cannot overpower (the being). ||9||
Whoever sings the Glorious Praises of the Lord's Name, O Nanak, is not affected by the world-ocean. ||9||
Whosoever recites God's Name and praises, him, the world ocean affects not, O Nanak.
Sri Guru ji says: those who, through the company of those saints, (ramanan) utter Hari's Name and virtues are not overpowered by the ocean of the world; meaning, they do not drown in the world. ||9||
1MAU: Gatha = praise (gatha = a religious verse). Goorr = deep (guh = hidden, concealed; guh = to conceal). Apaaran = the infinite (Prabhu) (apaar).
Singing the praise of the infinite Parmatma is a deep (and subtle) task; only a rare person understands it.
This Gaat'haa is profound and infinite; how rare are those who understand it.
Profound and infinite is the gospel of the Lord. Rare is the one who understands it.
This story of the infinite Vahiguru is supremely secret. Only a rare saint understands its conclusion. But the one who does understand — their state is told (next).
1VW5: Kaam = desire. Tajnan = (tyaj = to give up). Saadh sangamah = (saadhu sangam) the true company. ||10||
O Nanak! By remembering Parmatma while staying in the true company, the desires of the world can be given up. ||10||
They forsake sexual desire and worldly love, O Nanak, and praise the Lord in the Saadh Sangat. ||10||
They who understand it, O Nanak, abandon worldly love and recite the World-Lord's praises in the society of the saints.
Sri Guru ji says: to dwell on Gobind's virtues through meeting the saints, and to give up the (kaam) schemes of the world — meaning, to become free of vices — this is the hard thing. ||10||
W9YT: Sumantr = the highest mantra (sumantra). Kot = millions (koti).
The Guru's words are (such) a supreme mantra (that they) destroy millions of sins.
The Words of the Holy are the most sublime Mantra. They eradicate millions of sinful mistakes.
The saint's word is the sublime spell. Through it millions of sins are eradicated.
The words of the saints, which are the form of the highest mantra, destroy millions of faults. Hearing those words:
FDZG: Samooh = multitude (samooh). Dokh = sins (dosh). Dhyaanan = (dhyaan) meditation. Saadh = (saadhu) the Guru. ||11||
O Nanak! (Through those words,) meditation on Prabhu's beautiful lotus feet redeems all one's generations. ||11||
Meditating on the Lotus Feet of the Lord, O Nanak, all one's generations are saved. ||11||
Meditating on the God's lotus feet, O Nanak, all the generations are saved.
The one who meditates on Hari's lotus feet — Sri Guru ji says — that person redeems all their generations. ||11||
7Q1S: Mandar = house (mandir = a dwelling). Sainah = sleeping, living (svap = to lie down, to rest). Jen madhy = within which (yenaam madhye).
Only living in those homes is lovely where Parmatma's praise is sung.
That palace is beautiful, in which the Kirtan of the Lord's Praises are sung.
Beauteous is that palace, in which the Lord's praises are sung.
The (sainah) dwelling in which Hari's kirtan happens — that alone is a beautiful house.
NZSQ: The people who remember Parmatma become free (of the world's bonds). But, O Nanak, (this remembrance) is gained by great good fortune. ||12||
Those who dwell on the Lord of the Universe are liberated. O Nanak, only the most fortunate are so blessed. ||12||
They who recite the Lord's Name are emancipated. O Nanak; the very fortunate ones alone are blessed with this state.
Those who utter Gobind's Name are the form of liberation. Sri Guru ji says: but remembrance of Gobind is gained through great good fortune. ||12||
HVXG: Labdho = found (labdha). Sumito = the best friend (sumitra).
I have found Parmatma, that best of friends,
I have found the Lord, my Friend, my very Best Friend.
I have found God as my friend, yea, my good friend,
Hari the Friend is gained only from the saints, who are the best of friends. ☬ What is that Hari like?
E38J: Bidaaran = tearing, breaking (vid = to cut in pieces; vidaaran = breaking). Chito bidaaran = breaking the heart, heartbreak.
He shall never break my heart.
and He breaks not my heart ever.
He never (bidaaran) breaks the heart of those who love Him.
C171: Asthal = place (sthala = firm ground). Amito = immeasurable, that cannot be measured (amita).
and whose dwelling is of immeasurable weight,
His dwelling is eternal; His weight cannot be weighed.
He, whose abode and weight are unweighable,
The (tol) reflection on His dwelling-place, the true company, is immeasurable.
GN29: O Nanak! I have made Him the companion who stays with my soul. ||13||
Nanak has made Him the Friend of his soul. ||13||
him alone Nanak has made the friend of his heart.
Sri Guru ji says: that very Vahiguru I have made the friend of my soul. ||13||
ZGAK: Apjasan = disgrace (apayashas). Sat putrah = a good son (satputra). Simartaby = should be remembered (smri = to remember; smarati = remembers). Ridai = in the heart. Mantranah = teaching.
(Just as) with the birth of a good son (any past) disgrace (of the whole family) is washed away, (so, to escape disgrace in the next world,) the Guru's teaching should be kept settled in the heart.
One's bad reputation is erased by a true son, Who meditates in his heart on the Guru's Mantra.
Ill-repute is effaced by the true son, who in his mind contemplates the Guru's word.

Just as, through the birth of an excellent son, all the disgrace of former times is wiped away — so it is fitting to beget such a son, by whom every blemish goes. In the same way the Guru's mantra is surely fit to be remembered in the heart.
